questions.question: A pattern chart lists these numbers in order, and there is no picture to look at: 3, 7, 11, 15. The same rule is used every time. If the pattern keeps going, what is the next number?
questions.explain: First find the rule by subtracting two numbers beside each other: 7 - 3 = 4, so the rule is 'add 4', and 15 + 4 = 19. A common trap is using the first number, 3, as the rule and answering 18.

questions.question: These four numbers are written in a row on a chart: 40, 36, 32, 28. Nothing is shown as a picture; the numbers are all you need. The same rule is used each time. What number comes next?
questions.explain: This is a decreasing pattern: 40 - 36 = 4, so the rule is 'subtract 4', and 28 - 4 = 24. Watch out for going the wrong way and repeating 32, which is the number that came before 28.

questions.question: A chart shows the numbers 100, 125, 150, 175 written in order, with no diagram of any kind. The pattern grows by the same amount each step. What is the next number in this increasing pattern?
questions.explain: The step is 125 - 100 = 25, so add 25 once more: 175 + 25 = 200. A common mistake is jumping two steps ahead to 225, or switching to counting by 100s.

questions.question: A pattern chart has five spaces in a row. The numbers written are 6, 11, then a blank space, then 21 and 26. There is no picture. What number belongs in the blank space?
questions.explain: The rule is 11 - 6 = 5, so 'add 5', and 11 + 5 = 16 (check it: 16 + 5 = 21). A common trap is counting by 4 or 6 by mistake and landing on 15 or 17.

questions.question: Priya puts money in her jar every week. Her chart shows: week 1 $7, week 2 $12, week 3 $17, week 4 $22. If she keeps the same pattern, how much will be in the jar in week 6?
questions.explain: The rule is add $5 each week, so week 5 is $22 + $5 = $27 and week 6 is $27 + $5 = $32. The usual slip is stopping one week early at $27, or doing 5 x 6 = 30 and forgetting the pattern starts at $7.

questions.question: A rain barrel in Victoria is being emptied. The chart of litres left shows: day 1 is 950 L, day 2 is 850 L, day 3 is 750 L, day 4 is 650 L. If the pattern continues, how many litres are left on day 6?
questions.explain: This decreasing pattern subtracts 100 each day, so day 5 is 550 L and day 6 is 550 - 100 = 450 L. A common trap is doing 950 - 600 = 350 by subtracting 100 six times, but day 1 already has 950 L before any is used.

questions.question: An increasing pattern starts at 12 and follows one rule: 12, 21, 30, 39. What is the 7th number in this pattern?
questions.explain: The rule is add 9, so keep going: 48 is 5th, 57 is 6th, and 66 is the 7th. Careful with 9 x 7 = 63; that ignores the starting number 12, and 57 is only the 6th number.

questions.question: Liam writes this pattern in his notebook: 88, 80, 72, 64. Which statement names the pattern correctly and gives the next number?
options: Increasing pattern, add 8; the next number is 72
Decreasing pattern, subtract 6; the next number is 58
Decreasing pattern, subtract 8; the next number is 58
Decreasing pattern, subtract 8; the next number is 56
questions.explain: The numbers get smaller, so it is decreasing, and 88 - 80 = 8 gives the rule 'subtract 8': 64 - 8 = 56. The trap is naming the rule right but then subtracting carelessly and writing 58.

questions.question: Ava measures her bean plant every second day for science class. Her chart shows: day 2 is 8 cm, day 4 is 14 cm, day 6 is 20 cm, day 8 is 26 cm. The plant grows the same amount every single day. How tall will the plant be on day 9?
questions.explain: The chart skips days, so 6 cm of growth covers 2 days, which means 3 cm per day; day 9 is 26 + 3 = 29 cm. The most common mistake is adding the whole 6 cm for one single day and answering 32 cm.

questions.question: Sofia's chart of chairs set up in the gym reads 6, 12, 18, 24. She says, ‘The numbers double each time, so the next one is 48.' Which statement is correct?
options: She is wrong; the rule is add 6, so the next number is 30
She is wrong; the rule is add 6, so the next number is 36
She is wrong; the rule is add 8, so the next number is 32
questions.explain: Doubling only works from 6 to 12; check every gap, and 12 to 18 is add 6, so the rule is add 6 and 24 + 6 = 30. Also watch out for adding 6 twice and landing on 36.

questions.question: A Surrey school is shipping out the cans it collected. The chart of cans still left reads: end of week 1 is 1000 cans, end of week 2 is 750 cans, end of week 3 is 500 cans. If the same number is shipped every week, at the end of which week will 0 cans be left?
questions.explain: The pattern decreases by 250 each week, so keep listing: week 4 has 250 cans and week 5 has 0 cans. The common trap is stopping at week 4 when 250 are still left, so always carry the pattern all the way down to 0.

questions.question: A campground near Golden charges one booking fee plus the same amount for each night. The chart of total cost reads: 1 night $60, 2 nights $95, 3 nights $130. What is the total cost for 5 nights?
questions.explain: Each extra night adds $95 - $60 = $35, so 4 nights is $165 and 5 nights is $165 + $35 = $200. The big trap is doing 5 x $35 = $175 and forgetting the booking fee that is already built into the first number.
